headline: Five EU carbon-removal associations urge four ETS changes to unlock permanent CDR at scale
summary: Five EU CDR associations representing ~200 members set out four amendments to the Commission's July 2026 ETS revision (which would auction ~250M allowances over 2031–2040 and centrally procure an equivalent volume of permanent removals, ~48 Mt/yr by 2040 toward a 250 Mt goal) that they say are needed to deliver those volumes.
co2crc_note: EU ETS integration of permanent CDR sets demand-signal and methodology precedents that shape global removal markets Australia could sell into.
extractor_note: capacity_mtpa 48 is a policy procurement target (48 Mt/yr by 2040), not project capacity; 250 Mt is a cumulative goal.

headline: US Class VI permit backlog reaches 142 applications, slowing CCS
summary: Speakers at the US CO2 Summit said the federal EPA Class VI injection-well permit queue has climbed to 142 pending applications, a bottleneck lengthening US storage-project timelines even as more states pursue primacy.
co2crc_note: US permitting friction affects global project timelines and investor sentiment toward storage; limited direct Australian relevance.
extractor_note: 142 is a count of pending permit applications, not a capacity or money figure.

headline: Texas regulator reports a drop in Class VI applications since taking primacy, with long-term liability still unsettled
summary: The Texas Railroad Commission says new Class VI storage-well applications have fallen since it received EPA primacy in December 2025, while long-term stewardship and liability arrangements for closed storage sites remain unresolved.
co2crc_note: Post-primacy application trends and unresolved storage-liability rules are watched as a template for storage-stewardship regulation globally.

headline: Canada to build a framework opening carbon-removal credits to international buyers under Paris Article 6
summary: Ottawa announced it will develop a market framework allowing foreign buyers to purchase Canadian carbon-removal credits under the Paris Agreement, positioning the country's DAC and geological-storage capacity for cross-border credit exports.
co2crc_note: Cross-border CDR credit trade under Article 6 is a direct template for how Australia could monetise domestic removal and storage internationally.
extractor_note: Framework to be developed; no money committed, hence commitment_status 'announced'.

headline: Japan and Petronas agree to ship Japanese CO2 to Malaysia for storage from 2028
summary: Japan's METI, JOGMEC and Malaysia's Petronas signed an agreement at the 3rd Asia CCUS Network Forum in Hiroshima on 27 September to cooperate on transboundary transport and storage of CO2, targeting shipment of Japanese CO2 (power, cement, steel, shipping, refining) to offshore storage off Sarawak from as early as 2028, with an initial injection target of at least 2 Mtpa.
co2crc_note: A government-level SE Asia cross-border CO2 shipping precedent directly relevant to Australia's transboundary storage ambitions (Bayu-Undan, Australia-Japan) and to APAC storage-hub competition.
extractor_note: capacity_mtpa 2 is the stated initial injection target (>=2 Mtpa), a whole-chain transboundary volume, not a discrete new facility.

headline: US nonprofit names first recipients of an up-to-US$1m programme for DAC and super-pollutant abatement
summary: A Bay Area nonprofit intermediary selected a direct-air-capture developer and a super-pollutant-destruction company as the first recipients of a catalytic funding programme worth up to US$1 million, an early-stage award notable amid tighter US federal climate funding.
co2crc_note: Philanthropic catalytic finance filling gaps left by tighter US federal climate funding; minor direct Australian relevance.
extractor_note: Amount is an 'up to US$1m' programme ceiling for first recipients; recipients unnamed and source paywalled.

headline: Enbridge says it is open to community dialogue on its proposed Blue Point CO2 pipeline in Louisiana
summary: Enbridge said it remains committed to 'open, transparent dialogue' over the roughly 50-mile CO2 pipeline it plans to build from the Blue Point low-carbon ammonia plant in Ascension Parish, as landowners along the route raise safety and siting concerns echoing the 2020 Satartia CO2 pipeline rupture.
co2crc_note: CO2-pipeline social-licence dynamics and safety perceptions (post-Satartia) inform community-engagement practice for Australian CO2 transport infrastructure.
extractor_note: Enbridge classified org_type 'other' (midstream/pipeline operator); community-opposition framing drives negative sentiment.
